moat_against: Pure commodity price-taker — Henry Hub sets the price, no pricing power
Reserves deplete — owner's earnings must be reinvested in drilling just to stand still
Gas price volatility drives OE/share from negative (2024) to $7.46 (2025)
Appalachia takeaway/pipeline constraints and regulatory exposure
Long-term energy-transition demand risk for natural gas
moat_for: Largest independent US natural gas producer — scale across Haynesville and Marcellus
Low-cost acreage with more than 15 years of drilling inventory
Market-connected portfolio with LNG/export access and pricing premiums
Merger synergies — $500M in 2025, $600M targeted by end-2026
Investment-grade rating regained post-merger; debt being paid down
moat_justification: Scale and cost position are real — largest independent US natural gas producer with low-cost Haynesville/Marcellus acreage, >15 years of inventory, market/LNG connectivity and $500-600M of merger synergies — but it is a pure commodity price-taker: Henry Hub sets its price, reserves deplete and must be re-drilled, and OE swings with gas prices. That is a weak moat (4/10), not a moderate one.
name: Expand Energy Corporation
one_liner: Largest US gas producer, moat 4/10 — clears 15% only on a cyclically elevated TTM base (weighted IRR 15.2%, IV@15 $92.01 vs $90.80 price, no margin of safety); on the normalized median base it prints Tier C, so sized to C.
tier_override_reason: Weighted IRR 15.16% rests on the TTM base of $10.99/share, which is cyclically elevated (H1 2026 OCF legs well above H1 2025; Q2 2026 OCF and net income already down year-on-year) versus $7.46/share for the latest FY and a $3.62/share 3-yr median. The preliminary run on the normalized median base printed Tier C (weighted IRR 11.79%) even with far more optimistic growth starts, and the weighted IV@15 of $92.01 sits only 1.3% above the $90.80 price — no margin of safety on a commodity producer with a 4.87x scenario spread. Sized to the conservative end of the method range (C to B).
